examples.label: Set the node id to attack

notes: CVE-2018-7602 is authenticated - you need a live session cookie and the target node id, so it's a post-login escalation, not an entry point.

recommended.note: Foothold on the Linux host - start privesc enumeration

name: Drupalgeddon3 - Authenticated RCE (Metasploit)
description: CVE-2018-7602 authenticated RCE. Requires a valid Drupal session cookie and a node id; set rhosts/vhost/drupal_session/drupal_node/lhost then exploit.

defense.why_it_works: Drupalgeddon3 (CVE-2018-7602) is an authenticated RCE exploiting insufficient sanitization of the destination parameter in node deletion form actions. Any authenticated user with node deletion permission can trigger it.
defense.prerequisites: Any authenticated Drupal user session. Drupal 7.x < 7.59 or 8.x < 8.5.3.
defense.impact: Authenticated RCE as www-data. Meterpreter session enabling full server control and credential harvesting.
defense.detection: Authenticated request to node deletion endpoint with exploit payload in destination parameter. Metasploit User-Agent in HTTP headers. Outbound TCP from web server to attacker IP.
defense.artifacts: Web server access log (POST to node delete with malicious destination) | Meterpreter network session in SIEM | Drupal watchdog log (node delete action)
defense.splunk_spl:
index=sysmon EventCode=1 (ParentImage="*w3wp.exe" OR ParentImage="*httpd*" OR ParentImage="*apache*" OR ParentImage="*php-cgi*" OR ParentImage="*php-fpm*" OR ParentImage="*java.exe" OR ParentImage="*tomcat*")
| where match(Image, "(?i)(cmd|powershell|bash|sh|nc|python)")
| table _time, Computer, ParentImage, Image, CommandLine

index=web sourcetype=access_combined (method=POST OR status=500)
| stats count by clientip, uri_path | where count>3
defense.elastic_kql: event.code:"1" AND process.parent.name:(w3wp.exe OR httpd OR apache2 OR php-fpm OR java.exe) AND process.name:(cmd.exe OR powershell.exe OR bash OR sh OR nc OR python*)
defense.sentinel_kql:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("w3wp.exe","httpd","apache2","php-fpm","php-cgi","java.exe","nginx")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","bash","sh","nc","python")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
| sort by Timestamp desc
// Drupalgeddon3 (CVE-2018-7602) authenticated RCE via Metasploit
defense.prevention: Update to Drupal 7.59 / 8.5.3 or later. Restrict user permissions -- node deletion for admins only. WAF signatures for CVE-2018-7602.
defense.misconfiguration: Drupal running unpatched with authenticated users able to trigger the vulnerable node deletion handler.
defense.secure_config:
drush pm-update
# Restrict node deletion role assignment
# WAF: block exploit pattern in destination parameter
defense.evasion: Rename/obfuscate the uploaded webshell and delete it after use; prefer the app's built-in functionality (PHP filter / module) over dropping files; pace requests to blend with normal traffic.

validation.success_criteria: At least one behavioral detection fires within 60 seconds of attack execution
response_steps: Correlate alert with source host, user account, and timestamp
Review PowerShell Script Block / Module Logs, Sysmon, Windows Security Event Log, Web proxy logs for surrounding context (5 min before/after)
Verify whether the activity matches known administrative baselines or change windows
If confirmed malicious, isolate the host and escalate to incident response

explain:
Authenticated Drupal RCE via CVE-2018-7602 in Metasploit:
  use exploit/multi/http/drupal_drupageddon3   the module
Requires a valid Drupal session cookie and a node id, so set DRUPAL_SESSION, DRUPAL_NODE, VHOST, RHOSTS, and LHOST before exploit; it abuses the same Form API flaw as Drupalgeddon2 but on a path that needs authentication.
